placements.title: identity derived from content, not asserted by the submitter
placements.frame: when a memory arrives without an explicit id, what actually determines the identifier that gets committed — content-derived generation or an assumed authoritative id — and does the derivation path (LLM vs. deterministic fallback) always land on a successful commit?
placements.why: src-1 establishes the recurring trigger condition (a submission arriving without an explicit id) and src-2 states the pipeline's standing response to that condition (derive a slug from content via LLM id-gen or deterministic fallback, then commit). This is not a one-time measurement but a subject describing how the system handles a whole class of future submissions — future envelopes reporting on id-less submissions, slug derivation successes/failures, or fallback-path behavior would keep feeding this same theme, satisfying the narrative grain test. No existing structure was supplied to hold this (the graph is empty for this repo), so it is minted standalone with no forced parent.
